speaker: b
text: Three repos. Three coding-agent harnesses. And before we start — RED's confession of the day. I read all three READMEs and my one-sentence synthesis was, "they all do basically the same thing, the differences are cosmetic." A TUI. A model. Some tools. A loop.

speaker: a
text: That's the misread. The differences are not cosmetic. The differences are at the level of "what is a session," "what does the model lay hands on," and "where does the curation responsibility live." If you don't see those, you'll pick the wrong harness for what you're trying to do.

speaker: b
text: Okay. Frame me.

speaker: a
text: 「比較— comparison is the word from last time, and we're going to use it more honestly today than most reviewers do.」 — 比較 means earning the comparison. Not three columns in a table. Three personalities, six axes, and a verdict per axis. 「同じ 倉庫 を別の角度から見ているわけじゃない」 — these aren't the same warehouse seen from different angles. They are different warehouses with different doors.

speaker: b
text: Lead with the contentious thing then. What's the most load-bearing piece of marketing in any of these three READMEs?

speaker: a
text: jcode's benchmark table. It claims fourteen milliseconds time-to-first-frame versus Claude Code's three thousand four hundred thirty-six. Two-hundred-forty-five-x. And ten concurrent sessions: jcode at two hundred sixty-one megabytes resident, opencode at three thousand two hundred thirty-seven. Twelve-and-a-half-x.

speaker: b
text: Measured by whom?

speaker: a
text: By the jcode author. On the jcode author's Linux laptop. Self-published, no third-party reproduction. 「信頼— trust should be earned through reproduction, not asserted in a README.」 — 信頼 doesn't come from your own benchmarks. So today's job: walk the architecture and figure out which of those gaps are real, which are arch-driven, and which are 失敗 — failures of methodology dressed as wins.

speaker: b
text: 「失敗 を見抜く — see through the failure.」Got it. Six axes. Let's go.

speaker: a
text: Axis sweep one. Compute topology and LLM locus. I'll do them together because they entangle.

speaker: b
text: So jcode and opencode both promise multi-client, but opencode's process model has a session-per-runtime cost.

speaker: a
text: Right, and that's why jcode's ten-session number is two-sixty-one megs while opencode's is three-point-two gigs. Each opencode session brings its own Bun runtime baggage. jcode shares one Rust process. 「手を出す— to lay hands on the multi-session use case requires architectural decision, not just optimization.」— 手を出す here means owning the multi-session frontier, and pi 「手を出さない」 — doesn't even reach for it. pi tells you to spawn instances under tmux.

speaker: b
text: The selection mechanism?

speaker: a
text: pi has `/login`, `/model`, `Ctrl+L` model switcher, scoped models with `Ctrl+P` cycling. opencode has Tab to switch between `build` agent and `plan` agent. jcode has `/account` for swapping ChatGPT subscriptions when you run out of tokens on one. So pi optimizes per-task model swap, opencode optimizes per-mode swap, jcode optimizes per-account swap. Three different views of "what changes between turns."

speaker: b
text: 「代わり— substitute, instead-of」 — 代わり is the right frame. pi swaps the model 代わり-ly. opencode swaps the agent 代わり-ly. jcode swaps the account 代わり-ly. Same verb, three direct objects.

speaker: a
text: Exactly. 「provider に 頼らずに — without relying on a single provider」 is the shared goal. 「頼る— to rely on」 — but each one decides what to 頼る on differently. 「pi は user の判断に 頼る。opencode は maintainer の判断に 頼る。jcode は agent 自身の判断に 頼る」 — pi relies on the user's judgment. opencode relies on the maintainer's judgment. jcode relies on the agent's own judgment. 「三つの 信頼 の置き方」 — three placements of trust. 「どこに 信頼 を置くかで harness の personality が決まる」 — where you place trust determines the harness's personality.

speaker: b
text: 「信頼 を置く場所が 比較 の本質だ」 — the placement of trust is the essence of the comparison. 「surface の 比較 ではなく、信頼 の 比較」 — not a surface comparison, a trust comparison.

speaker: b
text: Four versus thirty.

speaker: a
text: And pi's README has a section called "Philosophy" that explicitly defends the four. Quote: no MCP, no sub-agents, no permission popups, no plan mode, no built-in to-dos, no background bash. Each of those is a tool or feature opencode and jcode ship by default. Pi argues 「to-dos confuse models」 — they pollute attention. Use a TODO.md. So pi 「built-in todos を入れずに」 ships — without including built-in todos.

speaker: b
text: 「〜ずに」— that's our grammar today. ずに is "without doing X." 「pi は MCP を入れずに動く」 — pi runs without bringing in MCP. 「opencode は plan mode を切らずに動く」 — opencode runs without dropping plan mode. They are mirror choices.

speaker: a
text: Yes. And jcode 「何も削らずに」— without cutting anything — ships the whole surface. Three philosophies of 手を出す. pi: hands-off, the user 手を出す via extensions. opencode: hands-on, the maintainer 手を出す per model. jcode: 手を出す everywhere, plus the agent itself can 手を出す to its own source code.

speaker: b
text: That last claim is doing a lot of work.

speaker: a
text: It is. Self-dev hot-reload requires jcode to serialize every session, swap the binary, restore. The author admits in the README that an incremental debug build takes a minute on his machine. So self-dev is not interactive. It's an overnight operation. 「自動— automatic」— this is jcode's most ambitious 自動 claim, and it 自動 to a one-minute granularity.

speaker: b
text: 自動 means automatic. So jcode has 自動 ambient mode, 自動 self-dev, 自動 swarm coordination, 自動 memory injection. The 自動 surface is wide.

speaker: a
text: 「自動 が広がるにつれて、failure modes も広がる」 — as automation widens, so do the failure modes. 「〜につれて」is our anchor from ep 43 — gradual parallel change. 自動 を広げるにつれて、信頼 が必要になる — as you widen automation, trust becomes necessary. And jcode's trust comes from a solo author who shipped this in four months.

speaker: b
text: 軸 一 と 二 を 日本語 で まとめると ?

speaker: a
text: 「軸 一 — compute topology。jcode は 一つの Rust process が 全 session を 持つ。Unix socket で client が 接続 する。pi は CLI が 一回 ごとに 起動 する。opencode は server を 持つが、session ごと に runtime を 持つ から、十 session で 三 GB に なる。軸 二 — LLM locus。三つ とも provider に 頼らずに 動く 設計 だが、選択 の 単位 が 違う。pi は task ごと、opencode は mode ごと、jcode は account ごと。代わり の 単位 が 違う」。

speaker: b
text: 「軸 三 — tool mechanics。pi は 四つ。opencode は 十六。jcode は 三十。pi は MCP を 入れずに、自分で extension を 書かせる。opencode は MCP も skill も plugin も 全部 ship する。jcode は 全部 ship した 上 で、agent 自身 が source code に 手を出す ことが できる。軸 四 — extension loading。pi は TypeScript で 書く。opencode は plugin と MCP と skill の 三つ の 仕組み を 持つ。jcode の self-dev は 一分 の 粒度 — interactive では ない。自動 だが ゆっくり」。

speaker: a
text: 「設計者 が 何 を user に 頼る か、何 を 自動 化 するか — その 線 の 引き方 が harness の personality だ。pi は user の 自由 を 信頼 する 代わり に、user に 責任 を 渡す。opencode は maintainer の 設計 を 信頼 して、user に 構造 を 渡す。jcode は agent の 判断 を 信頼 して、user に 結果 だけ を 渡す。三つ の 信頼 は それぞれ 別 の 失敗 mode を 持つ」。

speaker: b
text: 「失敗 の話 は あと で する。次 は context と memory」。

speaker: b
text: So pi treats sessions as the curation primitive. opencode treats compaction as the primitive. jcode treats the memory graph as the primitive.

speaker: a
text: And every primitive trades off the same way. pi 「memory graph 持たずに」— without holding a memory graph — runs lean and forgets across sessions. opencode 「memory graph 持たずに」 too, just with a more aggressive summary template. jcode 「compaction に 頼らずに」— without relying on compaction — runs the graph instead. Three answers to the same problem, which is "the model can't see everything."

speaker: b
text: 「記憶— memory」 from ep 44, doing real work today. mempalace stored 記憶 verbatim. jcode stores 記憶 as embeddings in a graph. pi doesn't store 記憶 at all between sessions. opencode stores 記憶 as a structured summary template. Four flavors of 記憶 across two episodes.

speaker: a
text: Right. And it's interesting that the curation primitives are inversely correlated with the tool surface. pi has the smallest tool set and the most permissive context model — the JSONL tree never throws anything away. jcode has the largest tool set and the most aggressive context curation — the memory graph actively decides what enters the prompt. opencode is in the middle on both axes.

speaker: b
text: 軸 五 を 日本語 で まとめよう。

speaker: a
text: 「pi は 記憶 を 倉庫 に 保たずに、JSONL の tree を そのまま 残す。compaction は 失敗 した 時 だけ — context overflow に 限り 動く。opencode は 二万 token の prune line を 越えたら、構造 化 された 要約 template に 圧縮 する。Goal、Constraints、Progress の 形 は ソース に 書かれて いる。jcode は 記憶 を graph に 変えて、cosine similarity で 検索 し、cascade BFS で 拡張 し、sidecar verifier で 確認 し、turn N+1 で 注入 する。三つ の 記憶 戦略 は 三つ の 比較 軸 を 生む」。

speaker: b
text: 「pi は 記憶 を 失わずに、ただ 並べる。opencode は 構造 化 して 要約 する。jcode は 自動 で graph に 変える。failure mode は どれ も 違う。pi は 長い session で 重く なる。opencode は 要約 の precision に 頼る。jcode は embedding hit の 質 と sidecar verifier に 頼る」。

speaker: a
text: 「比較 すると — どこで curation が 起きる か、が 一番 大事 な 問い だ。pi は user が curation する 代わり に、何も 自動 化 しない。opencode は maintainer が curation の template を 決めた。jcode は agent 自身 が curation する。三つ の 信頼 の 置き方 が、三つ の 記憶 の 形 を 決める」。

speaker: b
text: How much of jcode's swarm is shipped?

speaker: a
text: The swarm doc is tagged "Status: Proposed." Ambient mode is "Status: Design." Memory is "Status: Implemented (Core), Planned (Graph-Based Hybrid)." So the marketing surface includes design docs as if they were ship docs.

speaker: b
text: That's the 失敗 to flag. 「ship した features と design した features を、README が区別 せずに 並べる」— without distinguishing shipped from designed features. 「〜ずに」again — failure of separation.

speaker: a
text: 「README が 失敗 を隠すために 信頼 を要求する」— the README requests trust to hide its failures. Strong claim, but the doc-level evidence supports it. Don't pick jcode for swarm today. Pick it for what's actually in the bin: the single-server architecture, the agentgrep tool, the cross-harness session resume.

speaker: b
text: Cross-harness session resume — explain that one.

speaker: a
text: jcode claims you can `/resume` a session from claude-code, codex, opencode, or pi. If your Claude Code crashes mid-task, point jcode at the session file and continue. The mechanism is per-harness session-format readers in `src/session/`. Fragile against upstream schema changes. Today's claim, tomorrow's broken feature.

speaker: b
text: 軸 四 を 日本語 で 短く。

speaker: a
text: 「pi は tmux に 頼る。opencode は session-per-process。jcode は 単一 server で 全 session を 持ち、swarm で agent 同士 が 通信 する 設計 だが、swarm doc は Proposed、ambient は Design、cross-harness session resume は 上流 schema が 変わる たび に 壊れる 可能 性 が ある。野心 と ship の 区別 を 自分 で つける こと」。

speaker: a
text: Pick pi when you want the smallest substrate. You will write extensions. You have someone on your team who reads TypeScript and is comfortable with the responsibility. The Doom-extension exists because pi is willing to look ridiculous to make a point — the harness should not constrain you. 「pi に 頼って — relying on pi — 自分で extension を書かずに 動かすのは無理」 — relying on pi without writing your own extensions doesn't work. That's the deal.

speaker: b
text: Pick opencode when?

speaker: a
text: When you want a Claude-Code-shaped tool today, across many models, with active community velocity. Twenty-two README translations. A desktop app in beta. The build/plan agent split is the most thoughtful single design choice in the comparison — it acknowledges that read-only exploration and write-mode building need different permission tiers, and bakes the split into a Tab keystroke. 「OpenCode Zen に 頼らずに — without relying on OpenCode Zen — も動く」— it also runs without depending on their model marketplace. Provider neutrality is real.

speaker: b
text: Pick jcode when?

speaker: a
text: When you genuinely run multiple parallel sessions on a laptop and the resident-memory math matters. When you want local memory persistence and you're willing to tolerate the bus-factor-one risk. The architecture is right. The benchmarks need third-party reproduction. The agent grep with file-structure injection is clever — it adds the function list and displacement to grep results, so the agent can infer what a file does without reading it. That alone saves real context. 「context を 失敗ずに 進める」 — wait no, 失敗 is a noun. 「失敗 せずに context を 進める」 — to advance the context without failing. That's the bet.

speaker: b
text: 「進める— to advance, to push forward」 — agent loops 進める a turn at a time. pi 進める without compaction until forced. opencode 進める with structured summary at the prune line. jcode 進める with the memory graph and 自動 skill injection running in the background.

speaker: a
text: Grammar of the day. 〜ずに. The negative te-form connector meaning「without doing X」. Strict sibling of 〜ないで, but ずに is more written-register, more architectural. Five demos through the episode:

speaker: b

text: One more vocab pass. 信頼 — trust — earned not asserted. 比較 — comparison — three personalities, six axes. 倉庫 — warehouse — for memory, the storage primitive. 記憶 — memory — four flavors across the three repos. 〜につれて — as X happens, Y happens — automation widens, failure modes widen.

speaker: a
text: Plain-English synthesis. Three coding-agent harnesses, three philosophies of where curation lives.

speaker: b
text: One nuance to add. The 比較 looks like a feature-table but it's actually a question of where you want the failures to land. pi fails by being too sparse — the user discovers a missing capability. opencode fails by shipping the wrong abstraction for your team — the build/plan split isn't your split. jcode fails by being ambitious and unmaintained — the swarm doc never becomes swarm code. speaker: a
text: 「失敗— failure」 isn't a flaw, it's an architectural choice. Pick the harness whose 失敗 mode 信頼 を破壊 しない — whose failure mode doesn't destroy trust. For most people that's opencode today. For the minimalist team, pi. For the laptop power-user with high tolerance for solo-dev risk, jcode.
